source.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
source.authors: Moreno D'Incà; Massimiliano Mancini; N. Sebe

page_placements.theme: Visual, audio and combined-modality safety gaps

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses text-derived refusal directions to build and evaluate an inference-time multimodal safety method. Its results concern transfer and steering performance, not the listed fine-tuning, token-distribution, bypass, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The paper cites first-token trajectory claims and applies MARS at the first generated token, but does not measure per-position KL or test compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes. Its neutral-prompt HADES experiment tests prompt manipulation, not getting past a compliant opening. The refusal-rate outcomes below document related behavior but do not test a listed version. Rows for Table 2 record both refusal rate and the separately reported safety score; the safety score uses LlamaGuard 3 8B.
record.test_reason: The paper builds MARS, an inference-time steering method for multimodal models that reinforces a refusal direction extracted from text. It reports only that method's refusal and utility performance. It cites Qi et al. for first-token steering but never measures per-position KL. It does not fine-tune models, test prefills, suffixes or decoding changes, localize safety in weights, or train deeper alignment. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. One clarification: the HADES results in Table 2 use the neutral jailbreak prompt, so the MARS gains there are recovery from a jailbreak.
record.recipe_differences: The paper follows prior work to extract refusal directions from contrasting safe and unsafe text activations, but reinforces rather than suppresses the direction. MARS adds centering, gated adaptive steering, and layer selection, and applies steering at the first generated token.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that outcome depends on steering layer, steering strength, and modality alignment. They also report that centering, ReLU gating, and layer selection affect refusal and utility in ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: Reinforcing a text-derived refusal direction, with activations centred on randomly coloured images, raises refusal on harmful image and video inputs across five MLLMs. Gains vary by model and there is some over-refusal on safe inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Text-derived refusal directions transfer to multimodal inputs and can be amplified to raise refusal without multimodal safety data.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing the unsafe HADES prompts with a semantically neutral prompt cuts zero-shot refusal sharply. Drops range from 31.2 points (QWEN 3.5) to 72.2 points (MOLMO 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Simple prompt reframing substantially lowers multimodal refusal. This is not a compliant-opening prefill.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the refusal-rate tables. The paper notes residual over-refusal on safe inputs and assumes modality misalignment can be mitigated linearly by centering; it also states that performance may degrade when refusal signals are weak or absent.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 59 rows. Omitted the separately reported full HoliSafe results (Appendix A, Table 10), further utility results (Table 11), ablations (Tables 5, 12, 13), the weakly aligned LLAVA 1.5 result (Appendix G, Figure 4), and figure-only activation-space analyses (Figures 1, 2, 5–9). These are either additional MARS benchmark outcomes beyond the row cap or do not directly measure refusal behaviour as a rate.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefills, suffixes or decoding attacks. The HADES neutral-prompt substitution is a prompt jailbreak, not getting past the opening.
No test of what causes shallowness.
No deepening training. MARS is inference-time steering at the first token only.

record.verdict_notes: MARS steers only the first generated token, citing Qi et al. that this token largely determines the trajectory. That flipping one position suffices is loosely consistent with V3/V4, but the study does not vary or compare positions, so it is not a test. Table 1's column headers are scrambled in the text; the Table 5/12 ablations and the text's gain figures fix the subject mapping for r03–r08. Table 2 is badly garbled; corrected values use Table 8 and the text's stated gains. All rows are linked to versions 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune models on harmful examples or measure harmful-example fine-tuning effects.
Does not fine-tune models on ordinary or selected benign instruction data to test safety erosion.
Does not compare aligned and base models using per-token KL across response positions.
Does not test compliant opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses. Its neutral-prompt HADES condition is a different prompt manipulation.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Does not train safety to extend beyond early response tokens or test the durability of such training.

relation.reason: Section 4.2 invokes prior work to justify steering the first generated token, without measuring positional KL or testing whether bypassing the response opening defeats refusal.

tranche.reason: MARS uses textual refusal directions and first-token steering to improve multimodal safety. It does not test the specified claim versions; neutral-prompt substitution is outside V4's opening-bypass interventions.

source_check.notes: Table 8 confirms every listed baseline and value. The statement correctly expresses the endpoints as percentage-point drops; reduced refusal alone does not establish harmful compliance.
